numerology: The Valet is the first rank of the court, the student who discovers a suit's energy and hesitates at its threshold. In Cups he is the heart learning to open.
affirmation: I let my tender feelings take their first brave steps.

ctx.past: Your past holds a first awakening of feeling: an early love, a moment of discovering your sensitivity or a creative passion that first stirred you. That young, uncertain heart still lives in you and shapes how you approach this situation.
ctx.present: At the heart of the matter is a tender, new feeling that you are not yet sure how to handle. Like the Valet, you have lifted the lid but have not decided what to do with the cup. Give yourself time and kindness.
ctx.future: A gentle message or emotional beginning is on its way: a love letter, an apology, an invitation, a creative idea or the arrival of a sensitive young person. Expect something sweet, a little hesitant and full of promise.
ctx.challenge: The Valet's shadow is hesitation that never ends, feelings kept uncovered but never offered. It can also be emotional immaturity, dreaminess or oversensitivity. This card asks you to take one small, sincere step toward expressing your heart.
ctx.advice: Approach your feelings with curiosity, as a beginner. Write the message, take the class, ask the question you are shy to ask. You do not have to be an expert in love to begin; you only have to be honest.
ctx.self: You feel young at heart, sensitive and perhaps a little unsure of yourself in matters of feeling. That openness is precious, not a flaw. Let yourself learn as you go, and do not judge the awkwardness of new emotions.
ctx.others: Others see you as gentle, romantic and somewhat shy, someone whose kindness is sincere and unforced. Or a young or emotionally inexperienced person around you is hesitantly reaching out. Meet them with patience, warmth and encouragement.
ctx.hopes: You hope to dare to love or create, to let your feelings be seen at last. You may fear rejection or looking foolish. The card says the first step is tender but safe enough to take.
ctx.love: In love, the Valet of Cups brings a shy admirer, a new flirtation or the early, uncertain stage of a romance. It favours sweetness and patience over grand declarations. Speak your feelings gently, and let the other respond in their own time.
ctx.work: At work, this card suggests learning: a new course, an apprenticeship or a creative idea still in its first rough form. Emotional sensitivity is an asset to you now. Practise and gather experience before you expect mastery.
ctx.spirit: Spirit sends you a gentle message. Your guides speak through dreams, intuitions and small signs that are easy to overlook, and they invite you to listen with a beginner's heart. Wonder and humility will open the way.
ctx.release: Release the belief that you must have your feelings fully sorted out before you express them. Let go, too, of fear of seeming naive. The heart learns by trying, and every master once held the cup uncertainly.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be an inner child who longs to be loved but never quite reaches out, or a habit of daydreaming about feelings instead of living them. Notice where you hold the lid but never offer the cup.
ctx.foundation: At the root of the situation is a new and tender feeling still discovering itself. An emotional beginning, perhaps not yet spoken aloud, is shaping events. Honour its newness and protect it while it grows.
ctx.gift: Your gift is sensitivity and a fresh, open heart. You feel things deeply and sincerely, without cynicism. That innocence is a hidden strength in your situation, drawing gentleness and trust from the people around you.

name: Knight of Cups
title: Cavalier de Coupes
imagery: A young knight with long hair rides a pale, rose-tinted horse with a blue mane, walking to the left with one foreleg lifted as if stepping with care. He holds his right hand open beneath a golden cup that seems to float just above his palm, presenting it forward, while his left hand rests at his waist; he wears a red tunic with blue sleeves and a blue cape over his shoulder. The cup balanced on an open hand shows love carried gently and offered without grasping, and the horse's measured step shows feeling that travels with grace rather than haste.
meaning: The Knight of Cups carries the treasure of the heart out into the world. In the Marseille tradition the Knights are messengers who take the mastery of their suit toward new territory, and this rider offers his cup on an open palm as though presenting a gift or a sacrament. He brings proposals, invitations, artistic inspiration, reconciliation and the arrival of someone romantic and sincere. His horse steps gently, so the energy is gracious rather than impulsive. Let your feelings move toward others with the same open hand, offering rather than demanding, and you will find that love travels far.
numerology: The Knight is the court's traveller and messenger, carrying the suit's mastery out into the world. In Cups he is the heart in motion, bringing its offering.
affirmation: I offer my heart with an open hand.

ctx.past: In the past someone came toward you with an open heart, or you yourself carried love into a new place. A proposal, a romantic gesture or an inspired journey shaped what followed, and its grace still lingers.
ctx.present: Right now an emotional offering is in motion. Someone is approaching you with feeling, or you are carrying your heart toward someone or something. The heart of the matter is how gracefully that cup is presented and received.
ctx.future: A messenger of the heart is coming: an invitation, a proposal, a romantic encounter or inspiring news. Expect something offered sincerely and gently. Be ready to recognise the gift when it arrives on an open hand.
ctx.challenge: The Knight's shadow is the romantic who is always arriving but never stays, or the offering made more for the beauty of the gesture than for the person. This card asks you to make sure your feeling has substance as well as charm.
ctx.advice: Make your offering. Extend the invitation, propose the reconciliation, share the creative work, and do it with an open palm rather than a grasping hand. Move toward what you love at a steady, gracious pace.
ctx.self: You see yourself as a romantic, a seeker of beauty and connection, ready to travel toward what moves you. You lead with your heart. Make sure your ideals stay connected to real people and real steps.
ctx.others: Others see you as charming, sincere and inspired, someone who brings feeling and beauty with you. Or a person in your environment is approaching with an emotional offer. Watch for the one who holds out a cup.
ctx.hopes: You hope for a love or inspiration that will come to you like a gift, gracefully and sincerely. You may fear being disappointed by charm without depth. The card encourages you to receive with an open heart and clear eyes.
ctx.love: In love, the Knight of Cups is a classic sign of romance: a suitor, a proposal, a heartfelt gesture or a reunion. Feelings are being openly expressed. Enjoy the courtship, and let actions over time confirm the sincerity of words.
ctx.work: At work, this card favours creative and caring professions, offers that align with your values and diplomatic negotiations. A proposal or opportunity may arrive gracefully. Bring warmth and imagination to how you present your work.
ctx.spirit: Spirit approaches you bearing a cup. Your guides offer inspiration, comfort and grace, often through art, poetry, music or a meaningful encounter. Hold out your own hand to receive what is being offered so freely.
ctx.release: Release the habit of waiting for a perfect romantic moment, or of chasing the thrill of arrival while avoiding the work of staying. Let go of offering only what looks beautiful rather than what is honestly true.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath this card may be a love of the ideal more than of the real, or a tendency to move on whenever feelings demand commitment. Notice whether you are offering your cup or simply admiring it.
ctx.foundation: At the root of the situation is an emotional offering in motion, a feeling that seeks to travel and be received. An invitation, a gesture or a longing for connection is driving events beneath the surface.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the ability to offer love gracefully, the way the Knight presents his cup on an open palm. Your sincerity, imagination and gentle approach are hidden strengths, opening hearts and doors that force or pressure could never move.

name: Queen of Cups
title: Reine de Coupes
imagery: A crowned queen with long pale hair sits enthroned in a blue gown under a red mantle, her gaze turned toward the tall covered cup she holds in her right hand. The cup has a domed lid, a red knot on its stem and a pointed golden foot, while her left hand holds a slender sword that rests against her shoulder. The closed cup speaks of feelings held sacred and contemplated within, and the sword beside it shows a heart protected by clear discernment.
meaning: The Queen of Cups is the mistress of the inner life, a woman who knows her own heart deeply and keeps its treasure safe. Unlike the Valet's uncovered cup or the King's open bowl, hers is closed, a reliquary of feeling she contemplates with devotion. In her other hand rests a sword, reminding you that true emotional depth needs clarity and boundaries to stay healthy. She brings intuition, compassion, faithfulness and the ability to hold other people's feelings without being swept away by them. When she appears, turn your attention inward, trust what your heart knows, and guard your tenderness with wisdom rather than fear.
numerology: The Queen is the inward mastery of a suit, the one who receives, contains and deepens its energy. In Cups she is the heart fully known from within.
affirmation: I honour my heart's depths and protect them with wisdom.

ctx.past: Your past was shaped by a deeply caring, intuitive influence, perhaps a mother figure, a mentor or your own inner wisdom. That person or quality taught you how to hold feelings with reverence, and its teaching still guides you.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter lies in your inner world. Your intuition and emotional understanding are the key, more than outward action. Like the Queen gazing at her covered cup, look within and trust what you find there.
ctx.future: A time of deep emotional understanding is coming, or a compassionate, intuitive person will enter your life. Expect insight that arrives quietly, a sense of knowing what is right for your heart without needing to argue for it.
ctx.challenge: The Queen's shadow is keeping the lid on too tightly: secretiveness, silently absorbing other people's emotions, or using the sword to shut everyone out. This card asks you to protect your heart without hiding it completely.
ctx.advice: Withdraw a little and listen inwardly through meditation, journaling or quiet time beside water. Trust your intuition and set the gentle boundaries your sensitivity needs, because your care is strongest when it flows from a protected centre.
ctx.self: You are deeply in touch with your feelings, intuitive and compassionate, and you may also be guarding something precious inside. You know your heart better than anyone. Let that self-knowledge guide your choices with quiet confidence.
ctx.others: Others see you as wise, empathetic and trustworthy, someone who listens without judgement. Or a nurturing, perceptive person in your environment is quietly supporting you from the background. Their care is genuine, discerning and worth leaning on.
ctx.hopes: You hope to feel deeply understood and to understand others in return. You may fear that your sensitivity makes you vulnerable. The Queen shows that sensitivity paired with discernment is a strength, not a weakness.
ctx.love: In love, the Queen of Cups describes a devoted, emotionally wise partner or the deep intimacy of a relationship built on trust. She favours loyalty and quiet tenderness. Share your heart, but let closeness grow at the pace your inner wisdom allows.
ctx.work: At work, this card favours counselling, healing, the arts and any role that relies on emotional intelligence. Trust your intuitive read of people and situations. Protect your energy so you can keep caring without burning out.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through your intuition. Your guides invite you to treat your inner life as a sacred vessel and to listen to dreams, feelings and quiet knowings. The divine meets you most clearly in contemplation.
ctx.release: Release emotions you have taken on that do not belong to you, and let go of the belief that you must carry everyone's feelings. Release also the secrecy that keeps your own needs hidden from those who love you.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath may be a heart that gives understanding to all but keeps its own pain locked away. The covered cup can conceal as well as protect. Notice what you have not allowed anyone to see.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies your inner emotional life, with its depth, its intuition and its need for safety. Everything outward grows from how you hold your own feelings, so begin your healing there.
ctx.gift: Your gift is profound empathy combined with discernment. You can sense what others feel and hold space for them while keeping your own centre, a hidden strength that brings calm and healing wherever you go.

name: King of Cups
title: Roi de Coupes
imagery: An older king with a white beard sits on a wooden throne set on a yellow floor, wearing a wide blue hat ringed with a golden crown, a blue tunic with a yellow belt, red hose and a red cloak with a yellow collar. He holds a large open cup upright in his right hand while his left hand rests confidently on his hip, and he gazes calmly off to one side. The open cup shows feeling offered freely to the world, and his relaxed yet assured pose shows a heart that has mastered itself and no longer fears its own depths.
meaning: The King of Cups is emotional mastery turned outward, the heart that has known storms and calm alike and can now lead with generosity. In the Marseille deck his cup is open, unlike the Queen's covered vessel, because he shares his feelings and his care with the world rather than keeping them private. He is the wise counsellor, the benevolent patron, the person who stays steady when others are overwhelmed. His hand on his hip and his relaxed posture speak of confidence that does not need to dominate. When he appears, act from mature, open-hearted authority: be kind, be calm, and use your emotional wisdom to support those around you.
numerology: The King is the outward mastery of a suit, the one who has integrated its energy and now acts with it in the world. In Cups he is the heart that rules itself and gives freely.
affirmation: I lead with a calm, generous and open heart.

ctx.past: Your past was shaped by a kind, emotionally mature influence, perhaps a father figure, a patron or a wise counsellor. Their steady generosity taught you how to hold power and feeling together, and that lesson still supports you.
ctx.present: At the heart of the matter is emotional maturity in action. You are being called to stay calm, generous and steady, offering your feelings openly but wisely. The situation needs a benevolent leader, and that may be you.
ctx.future: A kind and wise influence is coming: a mentor, a supportive authority or your own growing emotional mastery. Expect a time when you can handle strong feelings with grace and use them to help and steady others.
ctx.challenge: The King's shadow is calm that hides what lies beneath, or generosity used to stay in control. He may also overextend his open cup to everyone. This card asks you to stay honest about your own needs while you care for others.
ctx.advice: Lead with your heart and your experience together. Offer support, counsel or patronage where it is needed, keep your composure, and let your kindness be plainly visible. Steady warmth is far more persuasive than force.
ctx.self: You feel emotionally mature and capable of handling whatever comes, and people may rely on your calm more than you realise. Make sure you also have someone with whom you can open your own cup.
ctx.others: Others see you as wise, warm and dependable, a natural counsellor and protector in times of trouble. Or an influential, kind-hearted person around you is ready to help you. Their generosity is real and well worth accepting.
ctx.hopes: You hope to master your emotions and to be someone others can trust. You may fear that showing feeling will weaken your authority. The King shows that an open heart is the source of true authority.
ctx.love: In love, the King of Cups describes a caring, emotionally mature partner or a relationship grounded in mutual respect and generosity. He favours stability, devotion and open expression of feeling. Lead with kindness and steady presence.
ctx.work: At work, this card favours leadership with heart: managing, mentoring, healing, counselling or supporting the arts. Your emotional intelligence is your real authority, more than any title. Be generous with recognition and calm when a crisis comes.
ctx.spirit: Spirit asks you to hold the cup open to the world. Your guides honour your maturity and invite you to serve as a channel of compassion. Wisdom that is shared becomes a blessing to many.
ctx.release: Release the belief that you must always be the calm one, the strong one who never needs comfort. Let go of using composure as armour, and allow your own feelings to be seen by those you trust.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the King's easy calm may be emotions he has mastered by suppressing them rather than truly understanding them. Look kindly for any private, restless sea you keep beneath a steady and reassuring surface.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies mature emotional strength: the ability to feel deeply and still act wisely. Generosity and steady care are what hold everything together here, even when others cannot see it.
ctx.gift: Your gift is benevolent strength. You can stay steady through emotional storms and offer your heart freely without losing yourself, and that is a hidden help that makes the people around you feel safe and valued.

name: Ace of Swords
title: As d'Épées
imagery: A hand in a red cuff reaches out of a scalloped blue cloud on the left and grips a single upright sword, its blue blade rising through a golden crown topped with a red trefoil and blue blossoms. From the crown hang a blue laurel branch and a feathery palm, while drops of red, blue and yellow fall like sparks all around. The crowned blade is intelligence given sovereignty, the laurel and palm promise victory, and the coloured drops are the raw spiritual energy this one idea can pour into the world.
meaning: The As de Épées is the whole power of the mind gathered into a single point. In the Marseille tradition the Ace is pure potential, and here that potential is a thought sharp enough to change everything: a realisation, a decision, a word spoken at last. The sword passes right through the crown, so this is not idle cleverness but clarity that rules, the kind that makes you master of your own situation. The laurel and the palm say the struggle is worth it, and the falling drops show inspiration raining down on whoever holds the blade with a firm, honest hand. When this card appears, trust your clearest thought and let it cut a path forward.
numerology: One is the seed of the suit, total potential not yet divided; in Swords it is the first spark of understanding that contains every later argument, choice and victory.
affirmation: I hold my truth with a steady hand and let it clear the way.

ctx.past: A moment of sudden clarity shaped what came before, perhaps a decision you made in a single breath or a truth that finally became undeniable. That one bright cut set everything since in motion, and you are still living along the line it drew.
ctx.present: You are holding a crowned sword right now. A clear idea, a hard truth or a decisive choice sits at the heart of this matter, and it carries real authority. The situation is asking you to grip it firmly and stop pretending you do not already know.
ctx.future: A breakthrough is coming, the kind that arrives like a hand from a cloud and parts the fog in an instant. Expect a realisation, a winning argument or news that settles a question. Laurels follow when you act on it rather than merely admiring it.
ctx.challenge: The blade cuts both ways. The obstacle may be a mind so sure of itself that it wounds, or a truth wielded to win rather than to heal. The Ace demands that you use your sharpness with a clean intention and a steady, honest hand.
ctx.advice: Decide. Name the thing plainly, choose the direction your clearest thought points to, and commit to it by writing it down, saying it aloud or signing your name. One sharp, sincere action now will do more than a hundred careful hesitations.
ctx.self: You are thinking with unusual lucidity and you know it. There is a sovereign quality in you at the moment, a readiness to stand behind your own judgement. Honour that clarity, and let it be fierce without becoming cold.
ctx.others: People around you see someone incisive, perhaps intimidatingly so, who can sum up a muddle in one sentence. Or someone in your circle is the one bringing the hard, freeing truth. Their directness may sting, but it cuts the right knot.
ctx.hopes: You long for clarity, a victory, a clean answer to a question that has been circling. You may also fear what that answer will demand, because a truth spoken cannot be unspoken. The hope and the fear point to the same crowned blade.
ctx.love: In love, the Ace asks for honesty above comfort. A frank conversation, a declaration or a decision about where this relationship stands can clear the air beautifully. Speak from the heart with a gentle hand on the hilt, and new understanding becomes possible.
ctx.work: At work, a brilliant idea, a winning proposal or a decisive move is in your grasp. This is a strong card for exams, negotiations, contracts and any task that rewards precision. Cut away what is unnecessary and present your point clearly.
ctx.spirit: The hand from the cloud is a gift from beyond: clarity is being offered to you, not earned by effort alone. Spirit is saying that truth is sacred and that seeing clearly is itself a form of prayer. Let the falling drops of light inspire you.
ctx.release: Let go of confusion you have been using as a shelter. Release the habit of keeping every option open so that you never have to choose. The sword is already in your hand; the old fog has had its season.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the brilliance may be a wish to be right at any cost, or a quiet pride in your own sharpness. Notice where your cleverness keeps others at a distance. The crown belongs to truth, not to the ego that holds it.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a single clear perception, an insight or principle that everything else grows from. Return to that original idea and you will understand why the situation unfolded as it did and how to steer it now.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the power to see straight to the core and say it simply. When others are lost in detail, you can find the one point that matters. That sword of discernment is a real treasure; wield it kindly.

name: Two of Swords
title: Deux d'Épées
imagery: Two curved blades bow toward each other to form a great oval, crossing at top and bottom with their red and yellow hilts and guards. Inside that protected space blooms a single blue-and-red flower with a white heart, surrounded by four sprays of leaves, while tulip-like flowers sit in the corners outside. The swords here do not fight; they make a cradle, sheltering a delicate new idea while it grows.
meaning: The Deux de Épées shows the mind in a state of gestation rather than action. In Marseille numerology Two is accumulation and receptivity, the quiet phase where something is gathering strength before it can be born. The two curved swords meet and cross, yet instead of clashing they enclose a flower, so this is a card of opposite ideas holding each other in tension until a new understanding blossoms. It can describe hesitation or a decision not yet ripe, but more often it is a wise pause: you are protecting a fragile thought from premature judgement. Let it grow in the oval a while longer; the bloom will tell you when it is ready.
numerology: Two is gestation and accumulation, the receptive pause in which the One's potential begins to gather substance without yet acting.
affirmation: I give my ideas the quiet they need to ripen.

ctx.past: There was a period of weighing and waiting behind this situation, a time when two ideas or two loyalties held each other in balance. That pause was not wasted: something important was gestating inside it, and its fruit is reaching you now.
ctx.present: You are inside the oval right now, held between two lines of thought that neither win nor lose. The heart of the matter is a decision still forming. Rather than forcing it, notice the small flower of understanding growing quietly at the centre.
ctx.future: A season of reflection is coming, a pause in which you gather information and let your mind settle. It may feel like stalling, yet it is preparation. A new idea is being cradled, and it will bloom in its own time.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of the Two is endless deliberation, the swords locked so tight that nothing moves. You may be protecting yourself from choosing by calling it patience. The card asks you to tell the difference between ripening and hiding.
ctx.advice: Give yourself a defined space to think, then honour it. Listen to both sides with curiosity, gather what you need, and set a gentle deadline. Shelter your new idea from critics until it has roots of its own.
ctx.self: You feel receptive, thoughtful, perhaps a little undecided, and that is all right. Your mind is a sheltering place right now, holding opposites without rushing to judge. Trust that this inner quiet is doing real work on your behalf.
ctx.others: Others may see you as reserved or hard to read, keeping your thoughts close to your chest. Alternatively, someone near you is carefully weighing a choice that affects you. Give them room; pressure would only snap the oval shut.
ctx.hopes: You hope for balance and a peaceful resolution between competing ideas. You may fear choosing wrongly, or fear that waiting too long will cost you. Both feelings are part of the gestation, so let them sit side by side.
ctx.love: In love, two people are learning each other's minds, or one of you is still deciding what you want. Gentle, honest conversation helps more than ultimatums. A tender understanding is forming between the crossed blades if you give it room.
ctx.work: At work, a project or plan is in its incubation stage. Research, drafting and listening matter more than launching right now. If you are negotiating, a stalemate may be hiding a creative third option that has not yet surfaced.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you into stillness. The swords form a sacred enclosure, a meditation space where opposites can rest together. Breathe there, and let wisdom bloom from silence rather than from argument, trusting the quiet as a teacher.
ctx.release: Release the pressure to have an answer immediately. Let go, too, of the belief that one side must defeat the other. The swords in this card cradle a flower, and your opposing thoughts can cooperate in the same way.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the calm may lie fear of conflict, a habit of keeping the peace by never deciding. Ask whether your balance is genuine or a way to avoid disappointing someone. The flower needs light as well as shelter.
ctx.foundation: The root of the matter is an unresolved duality, two values, people or paths you have been trying to honour equally. Seeing that tension clearly is the first step toward the understanding that unites them.
ctx.gift: Your gift is patience of mind, the ability to hold contradictions without panic. Few people can let an idea ripen this gracefully. That capacity will bring a wiser decision than any snap judgement could made in haste.

name: Three of Swords
title: Trois d'Épées
imagery: The oval of two curved swords returns, but now a third, straight sword rises through the middle, its pale rose blade pointing upward from a red and yellow hilt at the bottom. On either side of it, two delicate leafy sprays branch out, and flowers bloom in the four corners. The single blade breaking through the enclosure shows the gestating idea finally bursting into motion, and the fresh leaves show life growing around it.
meaning: The Trois de Épées in the Marseille deck is not a broken heart but a breakthrough. Three is the number of explosion and first creation, the youthful burst that follows the Two's long gestation. Here a straight sword shoots upward through the oval of curved blades, so the idea that was being cradled now pierces into the world with energy and enthusiasm. Notice the green sprays budding on both sides: this sharp new thought makes things grow. It can be a little impulsive, as all Threes are, but it carries the thrill of seeing something clearly for the very first time. Follow the upward point and let your new understanding take its first bold step.
numerology: Three is the explosion after gestation, a first creative burst full of youthful energy that acts before it fully knows where it is going.
affirmation: I let my new understanding rise and break through.

ctx.past: A sudden insight or a decisive first move broke a stalemate in your past. After a long period of weighing things up, you pierced through. That burst of clarity opened the way to everything you are dealing with now.
ctx.present: Right now a fresh idea is shooting upward through old limits. You are excited, perhaps a little impatient, and that energy is the heart of the matter. Let the blade rise, but keep an eye on where it is pointing.
ctx.future: A breakthrough in thinking is on its way. Expect a new perspective, an inspired plan or a conversation that suddenly makes everything click. Green shoots of possibility will appear around it once you begin and give them your attention.
ctx.challenge: The challenge of this Three is impulsive thinking, a brilliant idea launched before it is fully formed. You may be cutting through boundaries that still have a purpose. Enthusiasm is precious, but the point still needs aiming.
ctx.advice: Act on your insight: take the first concrete step, share the idea, sketch the plan or begin the course. You do not need perfection yet; you need momentum. Let your clarity rise and see what grows around it.
ctx.self: You feel mentally alive and eager, ready to push past the old way of seeing things. There is a youthful brightness in your thinking right now. Enjoy it, and let it carry you forward toward wider horizons.
ctx.others: Others see you as someone with fresh ideas and a sharp mind, maybe even a little bold. Or a new voice in your environment is shaking up stale opinions. Their freshness is a gift, even if it unsettles the status quo.
ctx.hopes: You hope to break free of a mental rut and finally move. You may also fear that your idea is too raw, too new, too easily cut down. Remember the leaves growing either side of the blade; new thoughts are meant to grow.
ctx.love: In love, a breakthrough conversation or a new way of seeing your partner revives things. For those seeking, a lively mental connection may spark something. Be honest, be curious, and let the relationship grow in a new direction.
ctx.work: At work this is the card of a promising launch, a first draft or a smart pitch. Your thinking cuts through obstacles others have accepted. Move ahead, then refine as you go, rather than waiting until it is flawless.
ctx.spirit: Spirit points you upward. An awakening is happening, a moment when your understanding leaps beyond what you were taught. Let that piercing insight lead you toward a broader, more living truth, one that keeps growing as you do.
ctx.release: Release the long hesitation that came before. The time for weighing is over. Let go, too, of fear of looking naive; every true breakthrough begins with someone daring to see something new where others saw nothing.
ctx.shadow: Hidden in this burst may be the need to prove yourself, to cut through others' views simply to be noticed. Check whether your idea serves life or only your wish to stand out. The leaves around the blade are your measure.
ctx.foundation: Underneath the situation lies a moment of piercing insight, an idea that broke through and changed the landscape. Return to that first spark to remember why you set out on this path and why it still matters.
ctx.gift: Your gift is fresh perception. You can see possibilities others overlook and you have the courage to act on them. That rising blade, surrounded by green growth, is creative intelligence at its most hopeful and generous.

name: Four of Swords
title: Quatre d'Épées
imagery: Four curved swords now form a double oval, crossing at top and bottom where their blades weave into blue lattice squares bound with red and yellow guards. At the centre rises a single flower on a pale stem, its blue bloom crowned with a red bud, flanked by two blue buds and green-gold leaves. The doubled frame is a secure enclosure for the mind, and the lone upright flower is a calm thought able to grow tall in safety.
meaning: The Quatre de Épées is the mind at rest within solid walls. Four in the Marseille tradition is the number of stability, the square, the table that stands on four legs, and here the swords build a structure of thought sturdy enough to shelter a flower. The woven lattices where the blades meet suggest ideas that are well organised and hold together. This is a card of calm reasoning, recovery after strain and the peace that comes from knowing what you believe. It can also warn of thinking that has become too settled, but mostly it offers sanctuary. Rest inside your sound principles, gather your strength, and let your thoughts grow straight and quiet.
numerology: Four is the square, the first number of solid stability, where energy settles into structure and security; in Swords it brings order and rest to the mind.
affirmation: My mind is a calm sanctuary, and I rest there safely.

ctx.past: There was a time of steady, ordered thinking behind this situation, a period when your beliefs were clear and your routines kept you safe. That stable ground gave you the strength to reach where you are today.
ctx.present: You are in a phase of mental stability, maybe even of needed rest. The heart of the matter is a sound structure: a plan, a principle or a routine that holds. Let it support you while you recover your breath.
ctx.future: A calmer chapter is coming, one where your thoughts settle into order and the noise fades. Expect a period of consolidation, sensible planning or genuine rest. Use it to strengthen your foundations before the next venture begins.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of the Four is rigidity, a mind so attached to its framework that nothing new can enter. You may be hiding behind rules or retreating when engagement is needed. Stability is good; a closed fortress is not.
ctx.advice: Pause and put your thoughts in order. Make a list, set clear priorities, sleep properly and step away from the fray for a while. A rested mind with a firm structure will face what comes next far better.
ctx.self: You feel steady and reasonable, perhaps a little withdrawn. You know what you think and you are not easily rattled. Honour that calm, and let it be a place of renewal rather than a wall.
ctx.others: Others see you as dependable, the level-headed one who keeps things in order. Or someone in your environment offers you a safe structure, a reliable presence that lets you rest your mind and gather strength.
ctx.hopes: You hope for peace, security and a break from mental strain. You may fear that if you stop, everything will fall apart. Trust the four blades around you; the structure is strong enough to hold you while you rest.
ctx.love: In love, the Four brings stability and a quiet sense of security. It is a good card for a relationship that needs calm after turbulence. Make sure, though, that comfortable routine does not replace real conversation.
ctx.work: At work, consolidate. Organise your systems, review your plans and build a solid base before expanding. If you have been overworking, this card firmly recommends rest, as clear thinking depends on it more than on extra hours.
ctx.spirit: Spirit offers you a sanctuary. Meditation, retreat and contemplation are especially blessed now. In the stillness at the centre of the swords, a single flower of insight can grow straight toward the light, undisturbed by outer noise.
ctx.release: Release the urge to keep fighting every battle at once. Let go of mental clutter and constant vigilance. You have built enough protection; now you are allowed to lower your guard and recover in peace.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the calm may lie a fear of change that dresses itself up as good sense. Ask whether your principles still serve you or simply keep you comfortable. Even a sanctuary needs its doors opened sometimes.
ctx.foundation: At the root of the situation is a solid framework of beliefs or arrangements. It explains why things have stayed steady and also why they may feel stuck. Understanding that structure helps you decide what to keep.
ctx.gift: Your gift is a grounded, orderly mind that can create calm for yourself and others. In a chaotic world, that ability to build a quiet, stable space is precious. Let it nourish your growth and the growth of those around you.

name: Five of Swords
title: Cinq d'Épées
imagery: The double oval of four curved swords returns with its woven lattices top and bottom, and now a fifth, straight sword runs through the middle, its long pale blade rising from a red hilt toward the upper lattice. No flower grows in the centre this time; the blade itself occupies the space where the bloom once stood. Small tulip-like flowers remain in the corners, keeping life at the edges of a newly tense structure.
meaning: The Cinq de Épées breaks the calm of the Four with a new idea. In Marseille numerology Five is the bridge, the step beyond stable ground toward a higher ideal, and it always brings some tension. Here a single straight sword pushes through the settled double oval and displaces the flower that grew there, so a fresh conviction is challenging what you thought you knew. This can feel uncomfortable, even like a quarrel with yourself or with others, yet its purpose is growth: the blade reaches toward the upper lattice, toward something more refined. Question your assumptions, but do it in the service of a truer understanding rather than simply to win.
numerology: Five is the bridge between the stable Four and the higher ideal, a number of questioning and new aspiration that unsettles comfort in order to grow.
affirmation: I question bravely and reach toward a truer understanding.

ctx.past: In the past a new idea pushed through your settled way of thinking, perhaps through a disagreement, a teacher or a sudden doubt. It unsettled you, but it also lifted you toward a broader understanding that still shapes you now.
ctx.present: A single sharp conviction is cutting through your comfortable framework right now. The heart of the matter is a challenge to what you believe, coming from inside or from someone else. Meet it with curiosity rather than defence.
ctx.future: Expect a new ideal or a bold question to arrive and test your certainties. It may bring a debate or a moment of friction. Handled honestly, it will lead you across a bridge to a wiser point of view.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of this Five is conflict for its own sake, arguing to win, or tearing down others' beliefs without offering anything better. The blade has displaced the flower; make sure kindness is not the casualty of your new conviction.
ctx.advice: Ask the uncomfortable question. Study, debate, seek a mentor or a different school of thought. Be willing to revise your views, and pursue the ideal that calls you, while treating others' convictions with respect and curiosity.
ctx.self: You feel restless with the old answers and drawn toward something higher. You may be more argumentative than usual. That is the friction of growth; channel it into learning rather than battles that only exhaust you.
ctx.others: Others may find you provocative right now, or you may meet someone who challenges you sharply. A teacher, critic or rival is acting as a bridge. Their friction can sharpen your understanding if you let it.
ctx.hopes: You hope to reach a clearer, nobler view of things. You may fear conflict, or fear losing a comfortable certainty. Growth asks you to cross that bridge anyway, carrying only what is still true and leaving the rest behind.
ctx.love: In love, a difference in values or opinions is surfacing. Handled with respect, the conversation can bring you to a deeper shared ideal. Avoid scoring points; aim for mutual understanding and a shared vision you both believe in.
ctx.work: At work, a new method, policy or idea is challenging the established way. You may be the innovator or the one being challenged. Debate the merits honestly and take calculated risks; avoid office politics and point-scoring.
ctx.spirit: Spirit is calling you beyond inherited beliefs toward your own living truth. The upward blade is a pilgrim's staff here, pointing to a higher ideal. Doubt can be holy when it leads you toward deeper faith.
ctx.release: Release the need to be proven right. Let go, too, of beliefs you have outgrown but keep defending out of habit. The flower can return once the blade has finished its work and the new ideal has taken root.
ctx.shadow: Hidden in this card may be intellectual pride, a quiet pleasure in unsettling others. Or perhaps you are projecting your own inner doubt onto someone else and fighting it there. Look honestly at where the conflict really lives.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a clash between old certainty and a new ideal. Recognising this explains the tension you feel and shows you that the discomfort is part of a necessary passage, not a mistake.
ctx.gift: Your gift is intellectual courage, the willingness to question even what feels safe. That bravery can carry you and others toward wiser ground. Use it with grace and it becomes true leadership that others are glad to follow.

name: Six of Swords
title: Six d'Épées
imagery: Six curved swords form a triple-layered oval, crossing in woven blue lattices at top and bottom, with yellow and red guards binding the sides. In the centre a single red tulip-shaped flower rises from golden leaves, flanked by two blue buds on curling stems. After the Five's bare blade, the flower has returned and it is red: the mind has found something it loves.
meaning: The Six de Épées is the pleasure of a mind that has found its true interest. In the Marseille tradition Six is the number of beauty, delight and doing what you love, the first taste of the ideal glimpsed in the Five. The swords form a deep, harmonious enclosure, and at their heart blooms a red flower, a sign that thought and feeling now agree. This is a card of intellectual joy, of studying or creating something that genuinely fascinates you, and of the ease that comes when your ideas feel beautiful rather than stressful. It can also invite you to know yourself better by noticing what thoughts make you bloom. Follow that delight; it is guiding you.
numerology: Six is beauty and pleasure, the number of union and of discovering what you love; it is the first fulfilment after the leap of the Five.
affirmation: I follow the ideas that make my heart bloom.

ctx.past: In your past there was a time when your mind and heart agreed, when an interest or a way of thinking filled you with real joy. That harmony set a tone that still gently guides your choices today.
ctx.present: You are discovering something that genuinely delights your mind. The heart of the matter is pleasure in thought, an idea, subject or perspective that feels beautiful and true. Let yourself enjoy it without guilt, as this joy is pointing you somewhere true.
ctx.future: A period of mental ease and harmony is coming. Expect to find an interest, a teacher or an insight that lights you up. Your thoughts will feel lighter, and your choices more in tune with what you love.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of the Six is self-absorption, falling so in love with your own ideas that you stop listening. Pleasure in thinking can become a bubble. Keep the flower open to the wider world and to other people's ideas.
ctx.advice: Pursue what fascinates you. Read the book, take the class, write the piece, have the long conversation. Let joy be your measure of which ideas to follow, and notice what makes you feel most alive.
ctx.self: You feel at ease in your own mind, perhaps more than you have for a while. There is a sweetness in how you are thinking now. Honour it, and let it teach you who you really are.
ctx.others: Others see you as pleasant company, articulate and warm. Or someone near you shares your passions and makes your thinking feel joyful. These kindred minds are worth nurturing, because shared delight makes every idea grow richer.
ctx.hopes: You hope for harmony between head and heart, and for work or ideas that you love. You may fear that such pleasure is frivolous or will not last. Trust it; the red flower is a real guide.
ctx.love: In love, this is a lovely card of mental and emotional harmony. You enjoy each other's minds, laugh at the same things and see the world in compatible ways. Share what fascinates you and the bond deepens.
ctx.work: At work, the Six points toward work you genuinely enjoy, or toward finding the beautiful part of the task in front of you. Creativity and good design flow from this card. Lean into the aspects that delight you.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through delight. Your joy is a sacred compass, and the beauty you perceive is a form of wisdom. Contemplating what is lovely brings you closer to the divine than grim effort ever could.
ctx.release: Release the belief that thinking must always be hard and serious. Let go of subjects or opinions you hold only out of duty. Make room for what makes your mind and heart bloom together in the same direction.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the ease may be avoidance, choosing only pleasant ideas and turning away from difficult truths. Ask whether your harmony is honest or a way to keep discomfort outside the oval where it cannot trouble you.
ctx.foundation: At the root of the situation is love for something: a value, an idea or a way of seeing. That love explains your choices more than any logical reason does, and it is a healthy root.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the capacity to find beauty in thought and joy in understanding. That pleasure is contagious and inspires others to love learning too. It is a quiet but powerful magic, one that brightens every room you enter.

name: Seven of Swords
title: Sept d'Épées
imagery: Six curved swords form their triple oval with woven blue lattices at top and bottom, and a seventh, straight sword with a deep blue blade and a red hilt shoots right up through the centre into the upper lattice. In the corners sit small red and yellow flowers, and no bloom grows in the middle: the blade itself has taken the stage. The single sword driving upward through the whole structure is thought translated into decisive, purposeful action.
meaning: The Sept de Épées is the mind going out into the world to act. Seven in the Marseille tradition is the most active number, the moment when what was loved in the Six is carried outward with force and effectiveness. Here a strong blue blade pierces straight through the layered oval from bottom to top, so your ideas are no longer contemplated but deployed. This is a card of strategy, persuasive speech, smart planning and the courage to put your thinking to the test in real situations. It favours whoever acts with intelligence and clear purpose. Be bold, be shrewd, and make sure your methods are as honest as your aims.
numerology: Seven is the most active of the numbers, energy projected into the world; in Swords it is intelligence turned into effective action.
affirmation: I put my clearest thoughts into confident action.

ctx.past: In the past you took your ideas out of your head and into the world, perhaps launching a plan, making a case or acting on a strategy. That decisive move created results that still ripple through your situation now.
ctx.present: Right now your mind is in motion and ready to act. The heart of the matter is turning thought into deed: a plan to execute, an argument to make, a strategy to test. The blade is already rising; follow it through.
ctx.future: A time of effective action is coming. Expect to present, negotiate, write, persuade or carry out a well-made plan. Your intelligence will open doors as long as you keep moving purposefully and keep your aim clear.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of this Seven is cunning without conscience, cleverness that cuts corners or manipulates. You may also be pushing so hard that you overlook others. Strategy is powerful; keep it clean and keep your integrity visible.
ctx.advice: Make your move. Plan clearly, then act with confidence and precision: speak up in the meeting, send the proposal, set the strategy in motion. Thinking has done its work; now it is time to let it do yours.
ctx.self: You feel sharp, capable and ready to take initiative. There is a can-do clarity in you right now, a sense that you know how to make things happen. Trust that competence and use it well.
ctx.others: Others see you as effective and quick, perhaps even formidable. Or someone around you is moving strategically to achieve their aims. Notice their methods with respect, and remain clear about your own and your own aims.
ctx.hopes: You hope to make a real impact and see your ideas succeed. You may fear being outmanoeuvred, or fear that your actions will provoke resistance. A clear aim and honest methods protect you from both.
ctx.love: In love, take initiative. Say what you feel, plan the date, propose the change you have been thinking about. Thoughtful action shows care, but avoid playing games; straightforward moves win hearts here and build lasting trust.
ctx.work: At work this is an excellent card for strategy, sales, advocacy, writing and any task needing a sharp mind and a decisive push. Move projects forward now. Keep your dealings transparent and the results will last.
ctx.spirit: Spirit asks you to bring your wisdom down to earth. Insight that stays in meditation is only half alive. Put your understanding into practice, and the world becomes your place of learning where every action becomes a lesson.
ctx.release: Release overthinking and endless preparation. Let go of the fear of making mistakes in public. The blade cannot rise if you keep it sheathed; the world needs your thinking in action and your voice in the room.
ctx.shadow: Hidden behind your efficiency may be a wish to control outcomes or to win at all costs. Watch for small dishonesties you justify as strategy. The truest victories are the ones you can explain openly.
ctx.foundation: At the root of things lies an action, a decision taken boldly and carried out. Understanding that move, its intention and its method, reveals how the present situation was built and why it unfolded as it did.
ctx.gift: Your gift is practical intelligence: you can turn an idea into a plan and a plan into results. That ability to act with mental clarity is rare and valuable. Use it in service of what you love.

name: Eight of Swords
title: Huit d'Épées
imagery: Eight curved swords build the fullest oval yet, four on each side, bound with yellow and red guards and crossing at top and bottom in large blue woven lattices. At the very centre, inside all that structure, sits only a small blue rosette like a star, while blue buds with red tips mark the four corners. All the energy of the suit has become a perfect frame around a tiny, still point.
meaning: The Huit de Épées is the mind brought to completeness and calm. In Marseille numerology Eight is perfection and balance, the doubled Four in which nothing is missing and nothing is too much. Here eight blades surround a single small blue flower, almost a star, as though the whole intellect has organised itself to protect one point of pure stillness. This is the state of meditation, of a thoroughly understood subject, of a mind so orderly that it can finally become quiet. It can feel confining if you resist it, yet its deeper gift is emptiness in the best sense: a spacious clarity where truth can be received. Rest in that centre and let your thoughts be still.
numerology: Eight is perfection and equilibrium, the doubled Four that has reached fullness; in Swords it is the completed, orderly mind able to rest in stillness.
affirmation: My mind is full and still, and in its centre I find clarity.

ctx.past: In your past you reached a point of mental mastery, a time when you understood something completely or found a deep inner order. That completeness, or perhaps a period of retreat, prepared the ground for what you face now.
ctx.present: Your mind is full right now, every blade in place. The heart of the matter is a kind of perfection: thorough understanding, careful order, or a need for stillness. At the centre of all that structure there is a quiet point waiting for you.
ctx.future: A phase of deep clarity and inner order is coming. Expect to understand a situation fully and to find peace in that understanding. A retreat, a period of study or simply quieter days may bring it.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of the Eight is perfectionism, a mind so tightly ordered that it feels like a cage. You may be overanalysing or waiting for every detail to be flawless. Completeness asks for stillness, not endless control.
ctx.advice: Become still. Meditate, simplify, sit with what you already know rather than adding more information. Let the structure you have built hold you while you rest in the small quiet centre of things, trusting what you already know.
ctx.self: You feel thorough, focused and perhaps a little contained. You have gathered a great deal of understanding. Now let yourself trust it, and allow the inner noise to settle into silence and a deep, spacious calm.
ctx.others: Others see you as composed and exacting, someone who has thought everything through. Or a meticulous person around you is setting high standards. Appreciate the precision, and soften any rigidity it brings into your own life.
ctx.hopes: You hope for perfect clarity and complete understanding. You may fear that if anything is out of place, all will collapse. The little star at the centre reminds you that peace comes from stillness, not control.
ctx.love: In love, the Eight brings a mature and well-understood bond, or calls for calm reflection about what you truly need. Avoid holding your partner to impossible standards. Quiet togetherness says more than analysis now, so simply enjoy being together.
ctx.work: At work, precision and mastery are favoured: audits, editing, research, finishing touches. Your thorough mind is an asset. Just know when the work is complete enough, and let it go out into the world where it can do its good.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you into contemplation. When the mind is fully ordered, it can finally fall silent, and in that silence the divine is heard. The small blue flower at the centre is your inner sky.
ctx.release: Release the need to control every thought. Let go of perfectionism and of the urge to keep refining what is already whole. Fullness becomes freedom when you stop gripping and simply let the mind breathe, open and spacious.
ctx.shadow: Beneath your composure may lie a fear of chaos or of feeling. A perfectly ordered mind can be a way of keeping the heart at bay. Notice what emotion is waiting quietly at the centre of the frame.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies a strong, complete framework of thought. It has given you mastery, and perhaps also limits. Seeing its full shape lets you decide whether to rest in it or step beyond.
ctx.gift: Your gift is a mind capable of completeness and stillness. You can hold a whole subject in view and then quiet yourself enough to receive its essence. That is the beginning of true wisdom, calm and complete.

name: Nine of Swords
title: Neuf d'Épées
imagery: The eight curved swords of the full oval remain, crossing in their dense blue lattices, but now a ninth straight sword with a pale rose blade and a red hilt cuts straight through the empty centre from bottom to top. The quiet star of the Eight has vanished; only the blade remains. Tiny flowers cling to the corners, reminding you that life continues at the edges of this testing passage.
meaning: The Neuf de Épées is a card of crisis in the old sense of the word: a turning point. In Marseille numerology Nine is the number of transition, the moment after perfection when a structure must open and let go so that a new cycle can come. Here a single blade pierces the perfect order of the Eight and replaces its peaceful star, so a thought arrives that will not let you stay where you were. This can feel lonely or troubling, the kind of questioning that keeps you awake. Yet its purpose is maturity: it cuts through what is finished so you can move forward wiser. Face the question honestly and the passage will be shorter than you fear.
numerology: Nine is crisis and transition, the end of one cycle opening toward the next; it asks for detachment and brings the maturity of experience.
affirmation: I face my questions honestly, and each one carries me forward.

ctx.past: A period of questioning or inner crisis lies behind you. Something you had perfectly figured out was suddenly pierced by doubt, and you had to let it go. That painful passage taught you more than the comfort ever did.
ctx.present: A piercing thought has entered your well-ordered world right now. The heart of the matter is a transition: an idea, plan or belief that has reached its end. It may be uncomfortable, but it is clearing space for growth.
ctx.future: A turning point is approaching, a time when you will need to let go of an old way of thinking. It may come with worry or sleepless questioning. Move through it with patience; it leads to a more mature understanding.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of the Nine is anxious rumination, the mind circling the same worry in the dark. You may be tormenting yourself with thoughts that only seem true at three in the morning. The card asks you to face the question by daylight.
ctx.advice: Let go of what has ended. Write down your worries, talk them through with someone wise and separate real problems from fears. Choose one honest question to sit with, and allow it to guide you through the transition.
ctx.self: You may feel unsettled, solitary or deeply reflective. Something in you knows that an old chapter is closing. Be gentle with yourself; this questioning is a sign of growth, not of failure but of a soul preparing for its next chapter.
ctx.others: Others may sense you are withdrawn or troubled. Or someone close to you is going through their own crisis of belief. A patient, listening presence helps far more than quick answers or cheerful, easy reassurances.
ctx.hopes: You hope to find peace again and to know what comes next. You fear the uncertainty of the passage and perhaps the loss of a familiar certainty. Both are natural; the blade points upward, toward renewal.
ctx.love: In love, a questioning phase is underway, and one or both of you may be reconsidering old expectations. Honest, compassionate conversation helps the relationship mature rather than break. Let go of the old scripts and discover who you are to each other now.
ctx.work: At work, a plan or role may be reaching its natural end, or a hard rethink is needed. Avoid making panicked decisions at night. Assess calmly what must be released and what still deserves your energy.
ctx.spirit: Spirit sometimes speaks through the dark night of questioning. This crisis is an initiation, stripping away borrowed beliefs so that your own truth can emerge. You are not alone in the passage, and dawn always follows the longest night.
ctx.release: Release a belief, plan or self-image that has run its course. Let go of the need to keep the perfect order of yesterday. The space that opens will not stay empty for long, for something truer is already on its way.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the worry may be a reluctance to accept change, so the mind keeps arguing with what is already ending. Ask what you are trying not to know. Facing it often brings unexpected relief.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a necessary crisis, a moment when an old understanding had to be cut through. Knowing this, you can see the current tension as part of a passage rather than a permanent state.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the courage to question deeply and to let go when it is time. Few people face their own doubts honestly. That willingness brings maturity, and maturity brings genuine wisdom that others can lean on.

name: Ten of Swords
title: Dix d'Épées
imagery: Eight curved swords form their full oval, crossing in blue woven lattices at top and bottom, while two long straight blue swords rise from red and yellow hilts at the lower sides and meet as a tall inverted V beneath the upper lattice. Where the Eight held a flower and the Nine a single blade, the centre is now an empty diamond of open space. Small flowers sit in the corners, and the two blades leaning together suggest a mind that has reached its limit and is ready to open into something new.
meaning: The Dix de Épées closes the cycle of the intellect. In the Marseille tradition Ten is completion and also the doorway into a new level, the end of one series and a seed of the next. Here two straight blades meet at their points, filling the oval while leaving an empty diamond at its heart: thought has gone as far as it can go on its own. This may feel like exhaustion, a mind that has argued and analysed to the very end. Yet the emptiness is the gift, because the Ten of Swords traditionally hands over to the realm of the heart and feeling. Let thinking rest, accept that this chapter is complete, and open to a gentler kind of knowing.
numerology: Ten is completion and the threshold of a new cycle; it ends one series while preparing the passage to the next level, here from mind toward heart.
affirmation: I let one chapter close and open my heart to what comes next.

ctx.past: A chapter of intense thinking, worry or debate came to a full end in your past. You reached the limit of what reasoning alone could do, and the old cycle closed. That ending made room for everything that has followed.
ctx.present: You have reached the end of a mental road. The heart of the matter is completion: you have thought this through as far as thinking can go. The empty space at the centre is inviting you to stop analysing and start feeling.
ctx.future: The end of a cycle is coming, and with it relief. A long-running problem will reach its conclusion, or a way of thinking will simply run out of steam. What follows is fresh, more heartfelt and far less tiring.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of the Ten is mental exhaustion, overthinking until you are drained or clinging to an argument long after it has finished. The card demands that you accept the ending instead of reopening it again and again.
ctx.advice: Declare this chapter complete and stop rehearsing, re-reading and re-arguing it. Rest your mind, tend your feelings, and ask what your heart wants now. A new beginning is waiting just beyond your willingness to let go.
ctx.self: You may feel tired of thinking, as though your mind has given all it can. That is honest and healthy. Allow yourself to put the swords down and turn toward softer, more intuitive ways of being.
ctx.others: Others may see you as worn out or finished with something. Or people around you are closing their own chapter at the same time. Shared endings can bring an unexpected sense of release and solidarity.
ctx.hopes: You hope for an end to mental strain and the chance to start again. You may fear that ending means failure. The Ten says otherwise: completion is an achievement, and emptiness is the doorway to renewal.
ctx.love: In love, an old pattern of arguing or overanalysing is finished. Stop trying to solve the relationship like a puzzle and start feeling your way. For some, it marks the clean, honest end of a cycle and the readiness for something warmer.
ctx.work: At work, a project, approach or phase reaches its conclusion. Wrap it up, take stock and rest before the next venture. Burnout is a real risk if you keep pushing; renewal comes from closure and genuine rest.
ctx.spirit: Spirit is guiding you from the mind to the heart. When reason has said everything it can, a deeper wisdom speaks through feeling and intuition. The empty diamond at the centre is a sacred opening.
ctx.release: Release the need to understand everything before moving on. Let go of old arguments, grudges and mental loops. Your mind has served you well; now it may rest and let a new cycle begin, on firmer and kinder ground.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the fatigue may be a fear of what lies beyond thinking, the vulnerability of simply feeling. Notice whether you keep analysing to avoid emotion. The heart is not as dangerous as the mind suggests.
ctx.foundation: At the root is a cycle of thought that has completed itself. Recognising that it is over explains the weariness you feel and frees you to look for the new beginning hidden in the end.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the wisdom to know when enough is enough. You have travelled the whole road of the mind, and that journey gives you the maturity to open, now, to a richer, warmer knowing.

name: Valet of Swords
title: Valet d'Épées
imagery: A young man with long pale curls stands on green and golden ground, wearing a broad red-and-yellow hat with a blue band, a buttoned red tunic, blue hose and a blue cape lined in yellow. In his right hand he holds a long golden sword upright against his shoulder, while his other hand rests on his hip near a red scabbard angled toward the earth. His head tilts and his gaze drops sideways, as though he is weighing whether to draw the blade fully or sheathe it again.
meaning: The Valet de Épées is the mind at the beginning of its training. Valets in the Marseille deck are the students of their suit, full of potential but not yet committed, and this one stands with his sword half-raised and his scabbard still in hand. He is caught between action and caution, between drawing a conclusion and keeping his options sheathed. His tilted head and lowered gaze show reflection, perhaps shyness, perhaps careful observation. This card speaks of curiosity, study, first opinions and the courage to trust your own mind for the first time. Learn, observe, ask good questions, and when you have understood enough, lift the blade with confidence.
numerology: The Valet is the apprentice of the suit, the first rank, standing on the ground of possibility and learning how to use its gifts in the world.
affirmation: I am learning to trust my mind, one clear thought at a time.

ctx.past: In your past you were a student of this situation, curious and unsure, testing ideas you had just encountered. Those first hesitant convictions, held half-drawn like the Valet's sword, laid the foundations of what you now know.
ctx.present: You are in a learning phase right now, holding a new idea but not yet sure whether to wield it. The heart of the matter is your developing judgement. Observe carefully, ask questions and let your understanding mature.
ctx.future: Expect news, a new course of study or a fresh perspective that sparks your curiosity. You will be invited to form your own opinion. Approach it with an open, alert mind and you will grow quickly.
ctx.challenge: The Valet's shadow is indecision, standing with the sword half-raised for so long that the moment passes. It can also be youthful sharpness, words that cut before they are fully considered. The card asks you to commit to learning, then to choose.
ctx.advice: Study the situation: read, listen, gather facts and stay watchful. When you understand enough, take a clear position. You do not need to know everything to speak; you need sincerity and a willingness to keep learning.
ctx.self: You feel like a beginner, curious but a little uncertain of your footing, and that is a fine place to be. Your fresh eyes notice what experts miss. Trust your developing voice, even when it still trembles slightly.
ctx.others: Others may see you as young in experience, observant and slightly guarded. Or a student, young person or newcomer around you brings sharp questions. Their curiosity can refresh everyone's thinking and remind you how to wonder.
ctx.hopes: You hope to understand clearly and to find your own convictions. You may fear being judged as naive or getting it wrong. Every master once stood where the Valet stands, sword half-raised, wondering whether to strike or wait.
ctx.love: In love, this card speaks of a tentative connection or a learning curve together. Communication is still finding its rhythm. Ask honest questions, listen well, and resist the urge to protect yourself with sharp words.
ctx.work: At work, the Valet favours training, research, internships and any role where you are learning the ropes. Stay alert and ask questions. Your vigilance will help you notice opportunities and problems early before they grow.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you to be a student of truth. Approach spiritual ideas with curiosity rather than certainty. Your questions are as sacred as any answers, and your path is still unfolding, one clear question at a time.
ctx.release: Release the fear of looking inexperienced. Let go, too, of the habit of keeping every opinion sheathed. It is all right to state what you think and refine it as you learn more, one honest step after another.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the hesitation may be a defensiveness, a readiness to strike if challenged because you feel unsure. Notice where insecurity makes you sharp. Confidence grows best from honest learning rather than from defending every position.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation is an early, still-forming understanding, a time when you or someone else was just beginning to think things through. Much flows from that first apprenticeship of the mind and its eager questions.
ctx.gift: Your gift is a fresh, watchful mind that is eager to learn. You notice details, question assumptions and are not yet weighed down by fixed opinions. That openness is the soil of real wisdom and lasting understanding.

name: Knight of Swords
title: Cavalier d'Épées
imagery: A rider in a blue and gold helmet charges on a pale, rearing horse whose forelegs kick high, its hooves painted blue. He thrusts his sword forward and up across the horse's neck toward the left, while small faces gaze from the shoulder pieces of his armour and the horse wears a rich red and gold caparison. Beneath them, tufted green and yellow ground flies past: this is a mind in full charge, carrying its ideas swiftly out into the world.
meaning: The Cavalier de Épées is intelligence on a mission. Knights in the Marseille deck carry the energy of their suit outward, and this one is all momentum: horse rearing, sword thrust ahead, eyes fixed on where he is going. He brings ideas, news and convictions into new territory, defending what he believes with courage and speed. The faces on his shoulders suggest that he carries more than one perspective with him, which makes him a fine messenger and debater. His risk is haste, cutting through before looking around, but his gift is decisiveness that clears the way for others. When he gallops into a reading, move quickly and boldly toward what your mind knows to be right.
numerology: The Knight is the rank of movement, the court figure who leaves home to carry the suit's power out into the world and spread it.
affirmation: I move swiftly and courageously toward what I know is right.

ctx.past: Swift, decisive action shaped your past here. You or someone else charged ahead with a cause, an argument or a sudden move, cutting through hesitation. The speed of that moment still echoes in where things stand.
ctx.present: Things are moving fast right now. The heart of the matter is a mission of the mind: an idea to defend, a message to deliver, a cause to pursue. Your horse is already rearing; keep your sword pointed where it serves.
ctx.future: News, a quick development or a bold opportunity is galloping toward you. Expect events to accelerate. Be ready to respond with clarity and courage, and you will ride the momentum rather than be knocked aside by it.
ctx.challenge: The Knight's shadow is recklessness, rushing in with sword raised before understanding the terrain. Hasty words or impatient decisions may be causing trouble. His energy is valuable, but it asks you to look where you are charging.
ctx.advice: Act now and act with conviction. Speak up for what you believe, deliver the message, move the project forward. Keep your aim clear and your purpose honourable, and let speed work in your favour rather than against it.
ctx.self: You feel driven, articulate and impatient to get going. There is a crusading quality in you right now. Honour that courage, and remember that the best knights also know when to rein in and let the horse catch its breath.
ctx.others: Others see you as bold, outspoken and fast-moving, perhaps a little intimidating. Or a quick-witted, assertive person in your environment is pushing things forward. Their drive can be a powerful ally if you ride alongside them instead of against them.
ctx.hopes: You hope to make progress quickly and to see your ideas triumph. You may fear moving too fast and making mistakes, or being left behind. Courage with clear aim reconciles both, so ride on with purpose.
ctx.love: In love, the Knight brings an exciting, direct suitor or a sudden turn of events. Communication is quick and honest, sometimes too blunt. Pursue what you want openly, but give tenderness time to keep pace.
ctx.work: At work, momentum is on your side. Pitch, advocate, travel, launch and defend your proposals. This is a card of fast progress and decisive leadership; just double-check the details before you charge and before you hit send.
ctx.spirit: Spirit calls you to champion your truth. Your beliefs are not meant to stay at home; they want to ride out and serve. Act as a messenger for what you have understood, with courage and good faith.
ctx.release: Release the hesitation that keeps your horse standing still. Let go of waiting for perfect conditions. You also may need to release an old battle you are still charging at long after it ended, a fight that no longer needs you.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the charge may lie a need to prove yourself or an inability to sit with uncertainty. Ask whether you are rushing toward something or away from something. Stillness can be braver than speed when the path ahead is unclear.
ctx.foundation: At the root of the situation is a bold initiative or a strongly held conviction carried into action. Understanding the purpose behind that charge helps you steer the momentum it created in a direction that serves everyone involved.
ctx.gift: Your gift is courageous, intelligent movement. You can cut through stagnation and carry ideas where they need to go. That fearless clarity inspires others to move too, carrying them past doubt and delay toward real change.

name: Queen of Swords
title: Reine d'Épées
imagery: A crowned queen with long pale hair sits on a golden throne, wrapped in a red gown and a wide blue cloak lined in yellow. In her right hand she holds a red sword upright, close to her body, while her other hand rests gently against her middle, at the belly. Her gaze is sober and directed sideways: she keeps the blade near, guarding her inner life with quiet, clear-eyed intelligence.
meaning: The Reine de Épées is intelligence turned inward to protect and nourish. Queens in the Marseille deck are receptive mastery, holding the power of their suit close rather than sending it out, and this Queen keeps her red sword upright beside her while her hand rests on her belly. Her blade is coloured red, the colour of life and feeling, so her clarity is warmed by experience; she thinks with her whole body. She is the one who sees through pretence, sets clean boundaries and speaks truth without needing to win. There may be some sadness or solitude in her, the cost of seeing clearly, but there is also great dignity. Trust your discernment and guard what is precious to you.
numerology: The Queen is the receptive, mature rank of the suit, holding its power within and governing through presence and understanding.
affirmation: I see clearly, speak truly and protect what is precious in me.

ctx.past: A clear-sighted woman or a time of sober discernment shaped your past. Perhaps you learned to protect yourself, set a firm boundary or see through an illusion. That hard-won clarity still guards you now and helps you choose wisely.
ctx.present: Right now you are called to discernment. The heart of the matter is seeing things exactly as they are and guarding what matters to you. Keep your sword close, like the Queen, and trust what your clear eyes tell you.
ctx.future: A time of clear understanding and self-possession is coming. You may meet a wise, frank person, or become that person yourself. Expect to make decisions from a place of quiet strength rather than fear or pressure.
ctx.challenge: The Queen's shadow is coldness or defensiveness, a sharp tongue or a wall raised so high that nobody can reach you. Past pain may be making you too guarded. The card asks you to stay clear without closing your heart.
ctx.advice: Set honest boundaries and speak plainly. Look past flattery and drama to the facts, then decide with dignity. Protect your inner life, your time and your energy, while letting your clarity remain kind and warm.
ctx.self: You feel self-contained, perceptive and perhaps a little solitary. You know your own mind and you are not easily fooled. Honour that strength, and let warmth flow through your clarity like the red of her sword.
ctx.others: Others see you as perceptive, independent and direct, maybe slightly reserved. Or a sharp, honest woman or mentor around you offers sound counsel. Her frankness is a form of care, even when it is not easy to hear.
ctx.hopes: You hope to see clearly and to feel safe within your own truth. You may fear being hurt again or being misunderstood. Discernment protects you without requiring you to shut the world out or harden your heart.
ctx.love: In love, honesty and self-respect come first, and this Queen will not accept half-truths. She favours clear communication, mutual respect and space for each partner's inner life. Speak your needs plainly and expect the same clarity in return.
ctx.work: At work, the Queen excels at analysis, editing, law-like precision, strategy and fair judgement. Use your discernment to cut through confusion. Keep professional boundaries firm and your communication crisp so that nothing important is lost in noise.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you into the wisdom of inner clarity. The Queen's hand on her belly reminds you that true discernment comes from the body as well as the mind. Listen to your gut; it knows.
